Recommendations: Prune affected leaves and apply organic treatments like neem oil.
Monitor closely for further signs of spread. Maintain proper spacing between plants for better airflow.
Consider using biological agents for early intervention (e.g., Bacillus subtilis, Trichoderma spp.).
Apply copper-based fungicides or bactericides to control bacterial spread.
Improve soil drainage to prevent waterlogging.
Remove heavily infected leaves and dispose of them away from the field to reduce further spread.
Remove severely infected plants to prevent disease spread to healthy plants.
Disinfect gardening tools (e.g., pruning shears, gloves) and any surfaces that may have come in contact with infected material.
Apply strong chemical treatments like streptomycin or kasugamycin.
Quarantine affected plants to prevent the disease from spreading to other parts of the garden.
Consider crop rotation with resistant tomato varieties or other crops not affected by bacterial spot.
